- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true prices often show sharper, delayed peaks or sudden drops.
- After a spike in history (e.g., 70+), model fails to adjust downward quickly; true prices often overshoot and then correct, or show mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Model exhibits strong upward bias in the first 5–10 forecast days, then flattens — true prices often show volatility and downward correction after initial peaks.
- Forecasts are too smooth; true prices show more abrupt changes, especially after 15–20 days, suggesting model under-captures short-term volatility.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in history, leading to persistent overestimation when true prices are falling.
- When true prices dip sharply after a spike, model fails to recognize the correction, continuing to forecast higher values.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, leading to over-forecasting of subsequent days — especially when true prices show mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Forecasts often lag behind true price movements by 3–5 days, particularly in the middle of the 30-day window.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price corrections after spikes — especially when true prices drop below 70 after a peak above 75.
